items.prompt: The pattern 2, 5, 10, 17, 26 continues in the same way. What is the 10th number?

figure.alt: A pattern: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, then an empty box.

options.why: Each number is 1 more than a square number.
Each number is 1 more than a square number, so add 1 to 10 × 10.

hints: Compare each number with the square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.
Each number is 1 more than a square number.
The 10th square number is 10 × 10.
items.explanation: The numbers are 1 × 1 + 1, 2 × 2 + 1, 3 × 3 + 1, and so on. The 10th number is 10 × 10 + 1 = 101.

items.prompt: The fractions 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 4/5 and so on follow a pattern. What is the product of the first 9 of them?

options.why: The 9th fraction is 9/10, so the last bottom number is 10.
9/10 is the 9th fraction, not the product.
Every fraction is less than 1, so the product is less than 1.

hints: Write out the product with all 9 fractions.
Each top number cancels with the bottom number of the fraction before it.
items.explanation: In 1/2 × 2/3 × 3/4 × ... × 9/10, each of 2, 3, ..., 9 appears once on top and once on the bottom, so they cancel. Only the 1 on top and the 10 on the bottom are left: 1/10.

solution.say: Cancel matching numbers on top and bottom.

items.prompt: Whole numbers are written in rows. Row 1 has 1 number, row 2 has 3, row 3 has 5, and so on. Row 1 is 1 and row 2 is 2, 3, 4. What is the middle number of row 12?

head: Row
Numbers
figure.alt: Row 1: 1. Row 2: 2, 3, 4. Row 3: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Row 4: 10 to 16. Each row has 2 more numbers than the row before.

options.why: 122 is the first number of row 12.
Row 12 ends at 12 × 12 = 144 and has 23 numbers.
The middle of 23 numbers is the 12th one.
144 is the last number of row 12.

hints: Look at the last number of each row: 1, 4, 9, 16.
Row n ends at n × n.
Row 11 ends at 121, so row 12 runs from 122 to 144.
items.explanation: Each row ends at a square number, so row 11 ends at 121 and row 12 is 122 to 144. That is 23 numbers, and the middle one is the 12th: 122 + 11 = 133.

solution.say: Row 12 has 23 numbers. The middle one is the 12th.

items.prompt: What is the last digit of 7 × 7 × 7 × ... × 7, with 2026 sevens multiplied together?

options.why: 1 is the last digit after a multiple of 4 sevens.
3 is the last digit after 3, 7, 11, ... sevens.
7 is the last digit after 1, 5, 9, ... sevens.

hints: Work out the last digits of 7, 7 × 7, 7 × 7 × 7, and so on.
The last digits go 7, 9, 3, 1, then repeat.
Divide 2026 by 4 and look at the remainder.
items.explanation: The last digits repeat 7, 9, 3, 1 every 4 sevens. 2026 = 4 × 506 + 2, so the last digit is the 2nd in the cycle, which is 9.

items.prompt: How many numbers are there in the list 13, 20, 27, 34, ..., 699?
hints: Find the jump between the numbers.
The numbers go up by 7 each time.
Find how many jumps of 7 take you from 13 to 699.
items.explanation: From 13 to 699 is 686, and 686 ÷ 7 = 98 jumps. 98 jumps join 99 numbers.

solution.say: Distance from the first to the last.

items.prompt: A ball is dropped from 160 cm. After each bounce it rises to half the height it fell from. How high does it rise after the 4th bounce?
hints: Halve the height once for every bounce.
After the 1st bounce it rises to 80 cm.
Keep halving: 80, then 40, and so on.
items.explanation: The heights after each bounce are 80, 40, 20 and 10 cm. So after the 4th bounce it rises to 10 cm.

items.prompt: The pattern 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 adds 2, then 3, then 4, then 5. What is the 20th number?
hints: The nth number is 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n.
The 20th number is 1 + 2 + ... + 20.
Pair 1 with 20, 2 with 19, and so on.
items.explanation: The 20th number is 1 + 2 + ... + 20. Pairing 1 + 20, 2 + 19, and so on gives 10 pairs of 21, which is 210.

items.prompt: 1 ÷ 7 = 0.142857142857..., where the digits 142857 repeat. What is the 2026th digit after the decimal point?
hints: The digits repeat in a block of 6.
Divide 2026 by 6 and look at the remainder.
items.explanation: The block 142857 has 6 digits. 2026 = 6 × 337 + 4, so the 2026th digit is the 4th digit of the block, which is 8.

items.prompt: The pattern 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 adds the two numbers before to get the next. How many of the first 30 numbers are even?
hints: Write O for odd and E for even under each number.
The pattern of odd and even goes O, O, E, O, O, E.
Every third number is even.
items.explanation: Odd + odd = even and odd + even = odd, so the pattern is odd, odd, even, repeating. Every third number is even, so the first 30 numbers contain 10 even ones.

solution.say: Why it repeats: odd + odd = even, odd + even = odd.
